Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: André Borchert
Message:
audit(#0045): keep libx264 primary for shorts and reject an oversized h264_videotoolbox primary

What: the youtube_short overlay no longer reorders the short encoder
ladder (default libx264 first, h264_videotoolbox fallback); it still
sets VT quality 65 and the tighter LUFS tolerance. validate() rejects an
h264_videotoolbox PRIMARY (main or short ladder) whose output exceeds
4096 pixels on either axis, naming the codec key, the size and the limit.
fast_preview, which keeps VT first for speed, now also sets the short
size to 1080x1920 (portrait counterpart of its 1920x1080 main render) so
it stays inside the limit. Tests cover the overlay order, both axes at
and just over 4096, VT as a fallback at 4320x7680, the main ladder, and
the fast_preview sizes.

Why: VideoToolbox cannot open an H.264 session above 4096 px per axis;
`ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=size=4320x7680 -frames:v 1 -c:v
h264_videotoolbox -f null -` fails with "Cannot create compression
session: -12903" (4096x4096 encodes, 4098x4096 and 4096x4098 do not).
With VT first at the default portrait size every short variant burned a
guaranteed-failing rung and a warning before libx264 ran, and
fast_preview's short render had the same latent failure.

Evidence: AUDIT/evidence/0045-before.log (Config.swift reverted: ladder
is VT-first, no rejection, fast_preview short size 4320x7680; 7
failures), AUDIT/evidence/0045-after.log (8 profile/config tests pass).
swiftlint 533/56.
